raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies inexpensive printed prompts and a predictable conversational routine. Seven frequent attendees value that routine, supporting its retention without establishing causality. A concrete limitation is five occasional attendees finding familiar partners' conversations difficult to enter; predictability may benefit returning learners while leaving entry unsupported. Slow pairing and partner changes are compatible with several explanations, including familiarity, proficiency or preference. Of 72 slips, 49 report sufficient useful practice and 48 identify preparation correctly, below the respective targets among respondents. There were 97 attendances; missing slips, untimed speech and unlinked responses limit conclusions. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. All evidence is stipulated synthetic observation.

openings.claim: Prior conversational familiarity may impede entry independently of proficiency; a self-contained opening exchange could preserve the helpful routine while improving access.
openings.delta: Keep the topic and pair practice, but begin with a brief printed exchange requiring no previous attendance, offering optional support prompts and extension questions without public proficiency labels.
openings.prediction: With pairs already formed, the entry exchange increases early speaking participation and reported usefulness among occasional attendees; pairing delays need not change.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary and self-contained openings across comparable rounds. Observe turn distribution anonymously and collect optional anonymous attendance-frequency and usefulness responses. Improvement after pairing would distinguish an entry barrier from pairing delay alone, although proficiency remains a possible moderator.
assumptions: Existing prompts can support both rounds within 75 minutes.
Preparation and observation can fit volunteer capacity; measure their cost.

openings.claim: Ambiguous task currency may contribute to earlier-task answers; explicit session dates could reduce that specific error.
openings.delta: Mark the existing printed sheet with one clearly dated next preparation task and make current copies available at every session, including to returning participants.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline, especially among print-only users; blank responses may persist if comprehension is the main barrier.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, tally correct, earlier and blank answers separately, optionally identifying print-only use anonymously. Log preparation queries and total coordination time; assess all original success measures rather than task accuracy alone.
assumptions: A next task can be selected before sheets are printed.
Dates are understandable; improvement remains a hypothesis until observed.

raw.assessment: The slips suggest shortfalls in useful speaking and preparation clarity, but incomplete, unlinked responses cannot establish participant-level effects. Entry difficulty may reflect shared conversational history as well as proficiency; neither cause is established. Coordination components remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: Conversational history may create an avoidable expertise imbalance. Retain the familiar session structure but restart each exchange around information only its current speaker knows: a personal experience, preference, or invented episode. The listener must discover and retell it before roles reverse; optional printed sentence starters support entry without public proficiency labels.
openings.delta: Make both partners alternately indispensable sources of new information, so regular attendance cannot supply all the conversational knowledge.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary prompts under the same pairing procedure, fresh-information exchanges should reduce reports of difficulty joining and increase useful speaking reports, particularly among occasional attendees. Persistent difficulty despite a fresh start would weaken the history explanation.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary and fresh-information prompts across pairs, reversing their order in another session. Use anonymous slips for entry difficulty, useful minutes, and optional recent attendance; observe whether both partners initiate turns. Track preparation effort alongside outcomes.
assumptions: Participants can choose a comfortable personal or invented subject.
Sentence starters can be adapted from existing sheets within the weekly coordination ceiling.
Benefits from novelty alone remain a competing explanation.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a printed six-date preparation menu with independent, reusable conversational tasks could prevent stale-task carryover while reducing repeated planning. Hand it out whenever someone attends; identify the next task by calendar date, and make preparation optional through an equivalent in-session starter.
openings.delta: Replace a preparation chain dependent on previous attendance with a persistent paper calendar that remains interpretable after absences.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers should fall without increasing blank answers; coordination savings should persist after counting initial menu preparation and printing.
openings.probe: Over six sessions, record next-task answers against actual dates and log all coordination minutes, including setup. Track useful speaking reports concurrently; check the stipulated 85%, 80%, and weekly under-90-minute targets using attendance counts and explicit missing-response counts.
assumptions: Dates and brief task descriptions are understandable to participants.
Independent prompts remain useful across current levels.
Menu creation fits within the first week's coordination limit; savings are unproven.

openings.claim: Self-contained printed openings with optional support/extensions may ease entry while preserving routine.
openings.discriminator: Post-pairing participation improves without shorter pairing delays.
openings.probe: Counterbalance openings; observe turn distribution and anonymous attendance-frequency/usefulness responses.
openings.uncertainty: Proficiency may moderate; adaptation and observation costs unknown.

openings.claim: Fresh personal or invented information, discovery, retelling and reversed roles may neutralize shared-history advantage; offer sentence starters.
openings.discriminator: Entry improves under unchanged pairing; persistent difficulty weakens history explanation.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary/fresh prompts across pairs, reverse order next session; observe both initiating, collect entry/usefulness/frequency slips and preparation effort.
openings.uncertainty: Novelty competes with history explanation; comfortable subjects and affordable adaptation assumed.

openings.claim: One dated next task on current sheets available every session may resolve task currency.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task answers fall; comprehension-related blanks may persist.
openings.probe: Six sessions: separate correct/earlier/blank answers, optional print-only use, queries and coordination minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Requires advance task selection and understandable dates.

openings.claim: A reusable six-date paper menu of independent tasks, distributed on attendance, may prevent carryover and repeated planning; provide equivalent in-session starters.
openings.discriminator: Earlier answers fall without more blanks; savings include initial setup/printing.
openings.probe: Six sessions: dated answers, speaking reports, all coordination costs including first week.
openings.uncertainty: Date comprehension, level suitability and savings unproven.

post_distill.decision: Probe separately; no established winner. All require free inclusive participation, no public proficiency requirement, paper access, conversational purpose, one room/75 minutes and no paid time. Evaluate original 80% speaking, 85% preparation and weekly under-90-minute targets using attendance denominators and missing counts. Synthetic evidence: 72 slips/97 attendances, untimed speech and unlinked responses limit inference; usefulness definitions, attendance causes and coordination components remain unmeasured.
